reductionDefinition: Karp's reduction converts each clause from a 3CNF into an OR gadgets to establish the truth assignments using labels.

reductionFrom.formalDefinition: GRAPHCOLORING = {<G,k> | G is a graph that has a k-coloring}
reductionFrom.problemDefinition: An assignment of labels (e.g., colors) to the vertices of a graph such that no two adjacent vertices are of the same label. This is called a vertex coloring.
reductionFrom.inputDescription: G, a graph, and k, the number of colors
reductionFrom.outputDescription: True or False, whether G has a valid k-coloring
reductionFrom.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionFrom.instanceFormat: Format: {((N,E),K) | N is set, E subset N unorderedcross N, K is int} Example: (({a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i},{{a,b},{b,c},{a,c},{d,a},{d,e},{a,e},{a,f},{f,g},{g,a},{a,h},{h,i},{i,a}}),3)
reductionFrom.certificateFormat: Format: {c1,...,cK} | color classes partition N, no edge in E has both endpoints in the same class Example: {{a},{b,d,f,h},{c,e,g,i}}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for the NP-Complete Graph Coloring problem
defaultSolver.complexity: O((numColors+1)^n * n^2 * m), n = |nodes|, m = |edges|, numColors = min(K, n)

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for Graph Coloring.

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: This is a default visualization for Graph Coloring

solver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for the NP-Complete Graph Coloring problem
solver.complexity: O((numColors+1)^n * n^2 * m), n = |nodes|, m = |edges|, numColors = min(K, n)

reductionTo.formalDefinition: SAT = {Φ | Φ is a satisfiable Boolean formula}
reductionTo.problemDefinition: SAT, or the Boolean satisfiability problem, is a problem that asks for a list of assignments to the literals of phi to result in 'True'
reductionTo.outputDescription: True or False, whether Φ is satisfiable
reductionTo.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionTo.instanceFormat: Boolean formula. Clauses joined by '&', literals within a clause joined by '|', negation prefix '!'. Each clause has 1+ literals of any size. Example: (x1 | !x2 | x3) & (!x1 | x2)
reductionTo.certificateFormat: Comma-separated variable:value pairs, optionally wrapped in parentheses. Booleans must be capitalized True/False (T/F also accepted); ':' or '=' may be used as the separator. List every variable you are assigning. Example: (x1:True,x2:False,x3:True)

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a simple brute force solver for SAT
defaultSolver.complexity: O(2^n * |phi|), n = number of variables, |phi| = formula size

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for SAT

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: This is a default visualization for SAT

solver.complexity: O(2^n * |phi|), n = number of variables, |phi| = formula size
